summary: Audit of the six scan/analysis figures against their captions (run_summary.html scan-section store for LuAG/XCET/Saturation; build_site.py lines 162/204 + scan narratives for DSB1/EJ199; build_runbook.py line 90 + r2829 store section for DriftStudy) and against the generating macros. Headline NEW findings, in severity order. (1) CRITICAL (EJ199): the timing trend curve in EnergyScanEJ199.png is a silently-broken fit — EnergyScanEJ199.C solves a/sqrt(E)(+)b through the 3&9 GeV medians (626, 249 ps), gets b^2 = -102,937 ps^2 (points fall FASTER than 1/sqrt(E)), clamps b to 0, and draws 1218/sqrt(E), a curve passing through NEITHER anchor and overshooting the 5/7/9 GeV medians by 5-20 sigma; meanwhile build_site.py:218 and FINDINGS.md:621 quote 1360/sqrt(E) and ModuleCompare.C:71 draws 1218/sqrt(E) — three inconsistent numbers, and the site claim 'trend fitting pure photostatistics' is contradicted by the figure. The faster-than-photostatistic improvement is itself physics (first-photon timing on a slow fluorophore scales ~1/Npe, supporting the contaminant hypothesis) and deserves to be stated, not papered over. (2) MAJOR: the narratives' showcase mean-vs-median rescues are invisible — the LuAG 11 GeV mean (547 ps) and DSB1 9 GeV mean (516 ps) are clipped above the timing-panel y-ranges (auto-ranged on the median graph only). (3) MAJOR (special-attention item): the three scan figures/pages are inconsistent about containment floors and tag thresholds — LuAG states only the 11 GeV floor 3800 (1-9 GeV use undocumented 60E+120); DSB1 states floors but misstates 1 GeV as '0' (actual 180) and never states its tag thresholds; EJ199 states NEITHER its floors (180/500/1200/1700/2200/2500, EnergyScanEJ199.C:154) nor thresholds; DSB1/EJ199 use cut 40 at 7 GeV vs LuAG's 50, undocumented, and only LuAG has an XCETScan figure. (4) MAJOR (SaturationStudy): the forensics intro's '(-3% at 9, -14% at 11 GeV vs linear)' is stale/wrong — the raw scan gives +8.4%/-12.6% and SaturationStudy_summary.txt gives +7.7%/-13.5% (centered); also the centrality panel's 9 GeV legend entry has zero plotted off-center points (its only bin, 10197+/-4901, fails the 12% error gate), so 'flat — no leakage ... per energy' is untested at 9 GeV, and the 5 GeV 'control is flat' claim is a -4.9+/-2.3% point. The four panels otherwise DO support the retired-saturation verdict, but two of the four narrative acquittals (per-capillary shares; time-of-day pattern) have no panel. (5) MINOR: cross-module anchor inconsistency (LuAG curve anchored 1&9, DSB1/EJ199 3&9) undermines the headline 'DSB1 constant term half of LuAG's 138 ps' comparison (LuAG re-anchored 3&9 gives ~421/sqrt(E)(+)127); DSB1 1 GeV median 366+/-4 sits ~8 sigma above its curve, unremarked; all three width/response panels plot 1 GeV points their tables decline to quote (ridge-merged); response-panel y-labels clip '10000'->'0000','12000'->'2000' in all three figures. (6) DriftStudy caption (build_runbook.py:90) is inaccurate on two counts: no 'pe rate' panel exists (the tail-pulse-rate discriminator that actually proves the light leak is absent from the figure) and the axis is hours-since-run-28, not wall-clock; the MIP panel's '(SiPM gain)' label contradicts the adopted conclusion that its +60% morning ramp is an estimator artifact; and the r2829 store still quotes 9 GeV sigma_t 212+/-11 / 'trend predicts 218', stale vs the adopted scan values 189+/-12 (median) and the 9-GeV-anchored trend. XCETScan caption is accurate; one stray red marker artifact at (~283, ~2.7%).

plots.what_it_shows: LuAG 4-panel energy-scan summary. TL: tagged-electron SumLG spectra at 1/3/5/7/9/11 GeV (counts in legend match the scan table: 5248/4129/1790/1200/522/187). TR: SumLG peak vs E with dashed linear-through-5-GeV reference (slope 592.4 ADC-eq/GeV); 11 GeV drawn open. BL: sigma/E vs E (157% at 1 GeV down to 18.5% at 11, non-monotonic 22.5%->31.9% at 7->9). BR: srCFD 4-cap shower-time sigma vs E, median (adopted) and mean (+0.12 GeV offset) points, teal curve 389/sqrt(E)(+)138 ps solved through the 1&9 GeV MEDIANS (verified numerically: 388.3/137.7).
plots.caption_issues: Store caption (run_summary.html scan section): 'Tagged-electron spectra, response linearity (dashed: linear through 5 GeV), width, and srCFD shower-time trend with the a/sqrt(E) (+) b curve.' Panel descriptions are correct. Completeness gaps: (a) MAJOR — the narrative's 11 GeV showcase ('edge-hit outliers drag the mean to 547 ps while the median holds at 227') cannot be seen: the 547 ps mean point is clipped above the panel's ~450 ps auto-range (frame set by the median graph only; EnergyScan.C draws gm 'P same' with no SetMaximum). The figure's central pedagogical claim is invisible. (b) MINOR — containment floors: only the 11 GeV floor (3800) is documented; 1-9 GeV use the formulaic SMIN = 60E+120 (EnergyScan.C:154-155), stated nowhere on the page, so 'e- on module' counts are not reproducible from the text. (c) MINOR — the open-marker-at-11-GeV purity convention is explained on the DSB1 page but not in the LuAG caption/narrative. (d) NIT — legend counts mix definitions: 187 at 11 GeV is the >3800 contained count, others are on-module counts.
plots.design_issues: Response-panel y-axis tick labels are clipped/overwritten: '10000' renders as '0000' and '12000' as '2000' (axis-title collision; same defect in all three module scan figures). Timing panel: no SetMaximum leaves the 1 GeV mean (440) at the frame edge and clips the 11 GeV mean entirely — set the y-range from BOTH graphs or annotate the clipped point with an arrow+value. Spectra x-range 0-16000 (shared cross-module scale, defensible, but LuAG data end at ~8000). Width and response panels plot 1 GeV points (157%, ~380 ADC-eq) that the scan table explicitly declines to quote ('ridge-merged') — either drop them or mark them open like the 11 GeV caveat points.
plots.physics_questions: (1) The trend curve is a 2-point closed-form solve (1&9 GeV), not a fit — the 3 GeV median (274+/-5) sits ~2 sigma above and 7 GeV (191+/-7) ~1.5 sigma below; a chi2 fit with the 11 GeV point excluded would give an honest parameter error on the 138 ps constant term. And why anchor LuAG at 1&9 when DSB1/EJ199 anchor at 3&9 (see DSB1 entry)? The 1 GeV anchor rides the material floor / ridge-merged spectrum. (2) Why is sigma/E non-monotonic 7->9 GeV (22.5 -> 31.9%)? '(sparse)' is noted, but the 9 GeV DQ subsample (522 e) is larger than the 11 GeV one (187) — is the run-9001 drift-period exclusion biasing the width? (3) Is 18.5% at 11 GeV comparable at all? The SumLG>3800 floor truncates the low tail of that peak alone; the apples-to-apples sigma/E with the other points' loose floors would be larger. (4) The raw 7 and 9 GeV response points sit ABOVE the linear-through-5 line (+16%, +8.4%) — the figure shows a night-run gain excess, not a 'high-energy flattening' until 11 GeV; the page narrative frames it as flattening (see SaturationStudy entry for the stale '-3% at 9' number).

plots.what_it_shows: DSB1 4-panel scan summary, same layout as LuAG. Spectra show ~2.1x the LuAG light and visible per-energy containment floors (3 GeV histogram starts abruptly at 1500, 5 at 2500, 7 at 4000, 9 at 6000, 11 at 6500 — matching EnergyScanDSB1.C:154); 9 and 11 GeV response points fall well below the linear-through-5 reference (-18%, -28%), consistent with the gain ladder + Longo migration + LG headroom ceiling story. Timing panel: teal curve 323/sqrt(E)(+)79 ps, verified as the closed-form solve through the 3&9 GeV medians (202, 133 ps); 11 GeV drawn open.
plots.caption_issues: Figcaption (build_site.py:162) 'Tagged-electron spectra, response, width, and srCFD shower-time trend for the DSB1 module' is correct but minimal. Narrative issues: (a) MAJOR — 'its 516 ps mean against the 133 ps median is the strongest daytime-outlier rescue yet' (build_site.py:176-177) points at a figure where the 516 ps mean is clipped above the ~370 ps y-range and invisible; only 3/5/7/11 GeV means are drawn. (b) MINOR — 'Containment floors 0/1500/2500/4000/6000/6500' (build_site.py:179): the '0' is wrong — SMIN_OV=0 falls back to 60E+120=180 ADC-eq at 1 GeV (EnergyScanDSB1.C:154-155). (c) MINOR (special-attention) — the DSB1 page never states its per-energy tag thresholds (cthr = 100/100/100/40/40/40, EnergyScanDSB1.C:103); note the 7 GeV cut is 40 here vs 50 for LuAG, so the LuAG XCETScan legend does not transfer, and no DSB1 XCET figure exists. (d) MINOR — the 1 GeV median (366+/-4) sits ~8 sigma above the drawn curve (332 ps at 1 GeV) with no remark; expected from the 1 GeV material floor, but a one-line note (as LuAG's narrative gives its 3 GeV tension implicitly via anchors) would pre-empt the obvious reader question.
plots.design_issues: Same y-label clipping in the response panel ('10000'->'0000', '12000'->'2000'). Timing panel y-range clips the 9 GeV mean (516 ps) — the panel silently omits 1 of the 12 points it purports to show. Width/response panels plot the 1 GeV ridge-merged point the table declines to quote. The 11 GeV response error (+/-734) is drawn but the open-marker convention is only explained in body text, not the caption or an in-figure legend entry.
plots.physics_questions: (1) The headline cross-module claim 'constant term nearly half of LuAG's 138 ps' compares a 3&9-anchored b=79 to a 1&9-anchored b=138 — re-anchoring LuAG at 3&9 gives ~421/sqrt(E)(+)127 ps, so the comparison direction survives but the quantitative ratio is anchor-dependent; fit both consistently. (2) Is the 9->11 GeV response flattening here separable into gain ladder vs LG headroom (~13.6k) compression? The 11 GeV spectrum visibly presses against 13-14k; a per-capillary rail/clip fraction vs E plot would quantify the ceiling contribution DSB1 uniquely suffers. (3) The correlated-capillary timing discovery (diagonal-difference upper bound) implies the 4-cap median here contains a common-mode component — does the 133+/-5 ps at 9 GeV decompose consistently with the ~75 ps ref-subtracted intrinsic already logged? (4) sigma/E non-monotonic at 9 GeV (26.5% vs 21.6% at 7) with a 6000 floor — floor-truncation bias again.

plots.what_it_shows: EJ199 4-panel scan summary. Spectra confirm the dimmest module (~550 ADC-eq/GeV); 7/9 GeV response points sit ~+16-21% above the linear-through-5 reference; 11 GeV response fit unstable (open point ~8600 with ~+/-2000 error bar). Timing panel: medians 1367/626/380/278/249/266 ps at 1-11 GeV with a teal curve that visibly overshoots every point from 5 GeV up by 100-200 ps.
plots.caption_issues: CRITICAL. The figcaption itself (build_site.py:204) is harmless, but the drawn trend curve contradicts both the plotted points and the narrative. EnergyScanEJ199.C (~lines 288-296) solves a/sqrt(E)(+)b through the 3&9 GeV medians, obtains b^2 = (249^2 - 1218^2/9) = -102,937 ps^2 — NEGATIVE — silently clamps it to 0 via std::max, and draws 1218/sqrt(E), a curve that passes through NEITHER anchor (703 vs 626 measured at 3 GeV; 406 vs 249 at 9 GeV, a ~9 sigma miss) and overshoots 5/7/9 GeV by 5-20 sigma. The narrative claim 'the trend fitting pure photostatistics (sigma_t ~ 1360/sqrt(E) ps, constant term unresolved)' (build_site.py:216-218) is wrong twice over: the drawn curve is 1218 not 1360 (1360 appears in FINDINGS.md:621; ModuleCompare.C:71 uses 1218 — three numbers in circulation), and b^2<0 means the data fall FASTER than photostatistics between 3 and 9 GeV, which is the opposite of 'fitting pure photostatistics'. 'Constant term unresolved' euphemizes an unphysical negative solution. Also stale copy-paste in the macro: the printout says '1&9 solve' while the code anchors 3&9, and the final printf says 'Wrote Output/scan/EnergyScan.png' for a file written to scan_ej199/. Secondary (special-attention): the EJ199 page states NEITHER its containment floors (actual: 180/500/1200/1700/2200/2500, EnergyScanEJ199.C:154, '~45% of expected peak') NOR its tag thresholds (100/100/100/40/40/40) — the only module page with neither documented; it quotes tag plateaus (88.7/22.8/5.6%) for the positive points only.
plots.design_issues: Same response-panel y-label clipping ('0000'/'2000'). The 11 GeV response point is plotted (open, huge error) while the table says 'fit unstable (low stats)' — table and figure disagree about whether the number exists. The 1 GeV width point (~46%) is plotted although the table gives no sigma/E at 1 GeV; it is also LOWER than the 3 GeV width (74.7%), a pure artifact of fitting the merged material-floor ridge, and will mislead at a glance. Timing y-range (0-1500) driven by the 1 GeV point compresses the 5-11 GeV region where the curve-point disagreement lives.
plots.physics_questions: (1) The real physics finding is being hidden by the broken fit: medians improve faster than 1/sqrt(E) from 3 to 9 GeV. For a slow fluorophore in the few-detected-photon regime, first-photon/threshold timing scales ~tau/Npe (i.e., ~1/E), not tau/sqrt(Npe) — a super-photostatistic trend is exactly what the contaminant-fluorescence hypothesis predicts, and would dovetail with the pulse-shape decay-constant fingerprint already 'in work'. Fit a/E vs a/sqrt(E)(+)b and report which wins. (2) Does the timing trend flatten between 9 and 11 GeV (249 -> 266 ps) because photostatistics saturate against the srCFD threshold floor, or is that the 11 GeV purity/statistics caveat? (3) Why do the 7/9 GeV EJ199 response points sit +16-21% ABOVE the linear-through-5 line when LuAG/DSB1 sit high at 7 by a similar amount — same night-run gain-ladder phase? If so the three modules share a beam-schedule systematic that a cross-module residual-vs-time-of-day plot would expose in one panel. (4) With ~275-550 ADC-eq/GeV and floors at ~45% of peak, what fraction of genuine electrons falls below the floor at 3-5 GeV, and does that bias the quoted peaks upward?

plots.what_it_shows: Two panels. Left: XCET40-AND-XCET43 coincidence rate vs software threshold per energy (log y), legend giving the chosen cuts (1/3/5 GeV: 100; 7: 50; 9/11: 40) with dotted vertical cut lines; 1-5 GeV curves plateau (85%/25%/~10%), 7-11 GeV curves fall without plateau. Right: XCET40 amplitude spectra per energy; the electron bump slides from ~700-850 ADC-eq at 1 GeV down into the sub-200 noise-adjacent region at 9-11 GeV.
plots.caption_issues: Store caption is accurate and unusually complete: plateau=clean-tag logic, 1/p^2 pressure scaling, dotted cut lines, and the peak-slide description all match the plotted content. Two completeness notes: (a) MINOR — this figure exists only on the LuAG page, yet the DSB1/EJ199 scans use a different 7 GeV cut (40 vs 50) and their pages carry no threshold documentation at all — either state the per-module cthr arrays in their narratives or generate per-module XCETScan figures; (b) NIT — only XCET40 spectra are shown for a two-counter coincidence tag; a one-line note that XCET43 behaves identically (or a mirrored panel) would close the loop.
plots.design_issues: Stray red marker artifact at ~(283 ADC-eq, ~2.7%) in the left panel, detached from the red 5 GeV curve (which ends at ~170) — looks like a mis-drawn point; worth fixing before external circulation. The three dotted cut lines at 40/50/100 are hard to associate with colors at a glance (the cut-100 line serves three energies); labels on the lines would help. Right panel: the sub-20 ADC-eq pedestal spike dominates the log-y range.
plots.physics_questions: (1) What accidental-coincidence rate underlies each working point? The run-30 book quotes 0.11% at 11 GeV; the equivalent number at 7 and 9 GeV (cuts 50/40 on falling curves) is the purity-defining quantity and is not shown — a singles-rate-product overlay would quantify it. (2) At 9 GeV the counters deliver ~3 pe (r2829 narrative) — the no-plateau curves here are consistent, but what is the tag EFFICIENCY (not just purity) vs energy? A 3-pe Poisson zero-fraction of ~5% per counter compounds to ~10% coincidence inefficiency, relevant to the e-fraction claims made from tag rates. (3) The 1 GeV plateau at ~85%: does this match T10 composition expectations at 1 GeV/c with the collimator+XCET-gas material in the line, and is the residual 15% muons/pions below threshold or geometry? (4) Why does the 5 GeV plateau droop ~11.5->8.5% across the threshold range while 1/3 GeV stay flat — the onset of the pe-statistics collapse, or a real mixed population at 0.4 bar?

plots.what_it_shows: Four-panel linearity forensics (SaturationStudy.C, runs 24/15/27/9001/30). TL: run-30 spectrum, all on-module tags vs centered (r<0.18) subset, centered peak 5885+/-218 vs scan-floor 5693+/-101 (+3.4%), with the 3800 scan containment floor marked. TR: peak(r)/peak(centered) vs centrality for 3/5/7/9/11 GeV — points at r~0.265: 3 GeV +7.7%, 7 GeV +4.5%, 5 GeV -4.9%, 11 GeV -8.9+/-9%; 3 GeV also ~1.00 at r~0.475. BL: MIP MPV 'gain ladder' under windowed+smoothed (~300-620) vs full-window-max (~900-1700) estimators — gross disagreement. BR: response vs E, raw scan (open) vs centered subset (filled), linear-through-centered-5-GeV and linear-x-Longo curves; centered residuals vs Longo +3.2/0/+19.6/+14.5/-5.5% (SaturationStudy_summary.txt).
plots.caption_issues: The store caption's 'clockwise' panel order is correct and panels TL/BL/BR are described fairly. Three problems: (a) MAJOR — the forensics narrative's framing numbers '(-3% at 9, -14% at 11 GeV vs linear)' (run_summary.html:~840s block) are stale/wrong: the raw scan gives +8.4%/-12.6% vs linear-through-5 and the study's own summary gives +7.7%/-13.5% (centered); no slope reproduces the quoted pair, and the sign error at 9 GeV inverts the story (9 GeV is HIGH, not low — the 'flattening' is an 11-GeV-only statement). (b) MINOR-MAJOR — TR caption 'peak vs impact centrality per energy (flat — no leakage)': the 9 GeV series has ZERO plotted off-center points (its only candidate bin, 10197+/-4901 with N=102, fails the 12%-error quality gate at SaturationStudy.C:286), so the legend promises a test the panel does not contain; and the '5 GeV tight-beam control is flat' claim is a -4.9+/-2.3% (2 sigma) point — better stated as 'the control shows the same few-% scatter, defining the method floor'. (c) MINOR — '11 GeV on the physics curve' is ~-5.5% (~1.5 sigma low), fair, but 'centered points scatter with time-of-day' is asserted with no time-of-day encoding anywhere in the figure. Net: the four panels DO support retiring saturation (centering does not restore the peak; the ladder is not a gain monitor; 11 GeV lands near linear x Longo), but two of the narrative's four acquittals — per-capillary share compression (test 2) and the time-of-day residual pattern (the verdict's positive evidence) — have no panel here.
plots.design_issues: TR panel x-axis runs to 0.8 while data end at 0.48 — half the panel is empty; and the 9 GeV legend entry should either be dropped or the panel annotated 'no off-center bin passes QC'. BL panel x-axis is unlabeled 'scan point 1-5' — mapping to runs 24/15/27/9001/30 (i.e., 3/5/7/9/11 GeV) is only in the macro. BR: a fifth marker style or color ramp encoding run start-hour would turn the time-of-day claim from assertion into evidence in one stroke. TL: the centered histogram extends below the 3800 floor (balance-validity floor is 2500) — honest, but a one-liner in the caption would prevent 'why is the teal below the floor line' questions.
plots.physics_questions: (1) The +19.6% residual at 7 GeV (run 27, night) EXCEEDS the +/-15% gain envelope the verdict quotes ('linearity established to the +/-15% cross-run gain envelope') — is run 27's implied gain excursion corroborated by anything independent (hall temperature log fragments, baseline RMS from Integrity_health)? As it stands the envelope is defined by the residuals it is meant to bound. (2) The missing test-2 panel: per-capillary energy shares at 5 vs 11 GeV are in the summary text (0.235-0.262 vs 0.223-0.271) — the 11 GeV TL/BR spread (0.223/0.271) is actually WIDER; is that beam-pointing drift at the T10 limit, and does it interact with the centrality normalization? (3) The Longo migration factors (0.968/0.940/0.916 at 7/9/11) assume a fixed sampling window — 'insensitive to the assumed module window' is claimed; over what window range was that checked, and does the capillary depth acceptance (not just tile stack) enter? (4) 3 GeV peak RISES +7.7% off-center (TR) — halo pions passing the tag at 3 GeV, or a genuine geometric effect (inter-capillary gap at center)? The same-sign +4.5% at 7 GeV hints at structure, not scatter.

plots.what_it_shows: Six stacked half-hour time series over ~11.5 h from run-28 start (23-24 slices): shower-time width ('the symptom', volatile 200-1450 ps with spikes at h~2, 4.5-5 and a sustained ramp after h~9.5); shower-time center (flat ~-1400 ps, +400 ps jump in the last slice); pooled HG MIP MPV (flat ~218 +/-1% for 8.5 h, then ramps to ~350, +60%); HG baseline RMS (flat ~50-55, doubles to ~100 after h~9); MCP amplitude (flat 902-919, +/-1%); trigger rate (185-213 Hz, supercycle-driven).
plots.caption_issues: Caption (build_runbook.py:90-92, mirrored in the r2829 store): 'MIP gain, pe rate, baselines and timing vs wall-clock — thermally stable box; the morning ramp is ambient light (sunrise/lights), not temperature.' Two factual errors: (a) there is NO pe-rate panel — the tail-pulse rate x2.4 jump that is the narrative's decisive light-leak discriminator is absent from this figure (as are the LG-vs-HG DC baseline shifts), so the figure alone cannot exclude the thermal explanation the caption dismisses: a correlated MIP-MPV + dark-noise ramp is exactly what a temperature swing would also produce, and only the MCP panel argues otherwise in-figure; (b) the x-axis is 'hours since run-28 start', not wall-clock — the sunrise interpretation needs the reader to know run 28's start time, which the caption doesn't give. MAJOR for standalone use: the third panel is labeled 'pooled HG MIP MPV (SiPM gain)' — but the campaign's adopted conclusion (r2829 narrative, FINDINGS) is that this morning rise is an ESTIMATOR ARTIFACT (peak-amplitude MIP fits swallowing noise maxima), not gain; the '(SiPM gain)' annotation asserts the retracted interpretation on the face of the figure. Also stale in the surrounding r2829 store: the 9 GeV results table quotes sigma_t 212+/-11 ps and 'trend predicts 218', inconsistent with the adopted scan values (median 189+/-12, mean 204+/-11, run 9001) and with the 389/sqrt(E)(+)138 trend that is anchored AT the 9 GeV median (predicting 189 by construction).
plots.design_issues: Six unlabeled-x middle panels (only the bottom carries 'hours since run-28 start'); fine for a stack, but adding a shaded band over the leak period (h~9-11.5) and a second band over the DQ-excluded slices would let the figure carry the story. A seventh panel with the tail-pulse rate (the actual discriminator) would make the caption true. Wall-clock ticks (or a top axis with CEST times) would substantiate 'sunrise'. The width panel's isolated spikes at h~2 and 4.5-5 are visually indistinguishable from the leak-period ramp yet have a different adopted explanation (near-threshold srCFD outliers dragging the per-event mean) — mark which slices the DQ cut removed.
plots.physics_questions: (1) Why does the shower-time CENTER jump +400 ps only in the final slice while the width ramp starts ~2 h earlier — is the leak-induced DC/baseline shift biasing the srCFD threshold crossing (amplitude-dependent walk), and does the median-combination recovery also restore the center? (2) The intermittent width spikes at h~2 and 4.5-5 correlate with nothing plotted (MIP, noise, MCP, rate all flat) — the adopted explanation is sporadic near-threshold outliers at the scan's smallest per-capillary light share; do these slices' spike amplitudes anti-correlate with the trigger-rate dips at h~4.5 (spill structure changing pile-up/halo mix)? (3) The MIP MPV is flat +/-1% for 8.5 h at fixed bias while the day-scale cross-run ladder is +/-15% — this figure is the strongest evidence that the ladder is DIURNAL (lighting + few-degree hall swings between runs), so would one overnight-anchored run per scan point (or the planned LED pulser) fully collapse the +/-15% envelope? (4) Was the 30-second lights-on/off baseline-RMS test proposed in the narrative ever executed at a later access — it would convert 'light leak' from inference to measurement.
